sections.html:
Manchester is the largest city in New Hampshire, on the Merrimack River, and shares the Hillsborough County seat with Nashua. The 2020 census counted 115,644 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 116,818. The city covers 34.93 square miles, 33.07 of them land. It lies 18 miles south of Concord, 18 miles north of Nashua and 51 miles north-northwest of Boston.

Healthcare, education, finance and technology anchor the local economy, and the old mill complexes now hold offices instead of looms. Manchester is a single school district and a single tax jurisdiction, so your neighborhood does not change your tax rate. It changes who is likely to buy, what the lot looks like and how close you are to the mills, downtown or the highway.

The 2010 Master Plan defines 25 neighborhoods. None has legal or political authority and only some have associations, but buyers and agents use the names, so they show up in listings.

  • West Side: Amoskeag, Rimmon Heights, Notre Dame and McGregorville, and Piscataquog (Granite Square)
  • East Side: North End, Janeville and Corey Square, Hallsville, and Bakersville
  • Periphery: Youngsville and Goffes Falls

Textile mills built much of Manchester, and the Amoskeag Manufacturing Company's company town was founded on the eastern bank in 1838. Many houses near the old mills date from that boom, including multi-family buildings. An older multi-family building can bring deferred repairs and tenant questions into the same sale, so sort out leases and maintenance records before you talk price.

Manchester's 2025 tax rate is $20.24 per $1,000, and the 2025 assessment ratio is 64.8%. The rate has four parts.

2025 tax rate components
Part of the rateRate per $1,000
Municipal10.04
County1.36
Local education7.33
State education1.51
Total20.24

The tax year runs April 1 to March 31, and bills go out twice. The first is mailed in late May or early June and the second in mid to late November, each due 30 days after mailing. The first bill uses half of the prior year's rate. The state sets the new rate in October or November, ahead of the second bill.

sections.h2: What happens when Manchester taxes are not paid
sections.html:
Manchester charges 8% a year on delinquent taxes under RSA 76:13, and unpaid balances can move to a lien. A notice of impending lien goes out by certified mail at least 30 days before the lien is executed, and interest then runs at 14% a year.

If taxes stay unpaid two years after the lien, the tax collector can execute a tax deed to the city under RSA 80:76. A former owner who wants to buy the property back after the deed must pay back taxes, interest, costs and a penalty of 10% of the equalized assessed value. The city also charges $10 per property for lien-release research and $2 per receipt.

Selling before a lien is executed avoids the 14% rate and the deed risk. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff and give it to your closing agent.

The city requires every residential rental property to have a Certificate of Compliance under Chapter 150, the Housing Code, of its Code of Ordinances. An application is required for any new, vacant or previously owner-occupied residential rental that is to be rented or offered for rent.

If you own a rental with a valid certificate and sell it, a Transfer of Ownership form assigns the certificate to the new owner. The Building Department asks for the form with a $50 check payable to the City of Manchester and does not take these applications electronically. Housing inspections are by appointment only, at 603-624-6450.

A buyer who wants to rent the house has to deal with the certificate, so confirm yours is current before you list.

The Merrimack and Piscataquog rivers and Cohas Brook drain the city, and the rivers have flooded before. New Hampshire's seller disclosure form asks about flood hazard zones, so if your house is near the water, check its flood zone status before you answer that question.

Interstates 93 and 293 meet near the Mall of New Hampshire. Manchester-Boston Regional Airport is in the city, the Manchester Transit Authority runs local buses, and Zip Line express routes reach Concord, Nashua and Salem. Easy highway and airport access is a real selling point for a house here.

sections.h2: Closing costs, disclosures and assessment appeals
sections.html:
New Hampshire's real estate transfer tax is $.75 per $100 of the price and falls on both buyer and seller under RSA 78-B. It is filed through Granite Tax Connect. Your closing agent will list your share on the settlement statement.

The seller of a one to four family home must disclose, in writing, the private water and sewage systems, insulation, any federally designated flood hazard zone and any underground heating oil tank, under RSA 477:4-d.

If you think your assessment is too high, the abatement application is due to the city by March 1 after the final bill, and an appeal must be filed by September 1. Gather recent comparable sales before you file.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Manchester
sections.html:
A cash sale lets a Manchester owner sell the house as-is, skipping repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal. You share details, receive an offer and decide whether to accept.

The title search, the tax proration and the state's transfer tax and disclosure rules still apply. Landlords should also confirm the rental certificate status, and anyone behind on taxes should get a payoff letter first. With those items ready, the closing can move as fast as you want it to.

faqs.q: What is Manchester's 2025 property tax rate?
faqs.a: It is $20.24 per $1,000 of assessed value, made up of $10.04 municipal, $1.36 county, $7.33 local education and $1.51 state education. The 2025 assessment ratio is 64.8%.

faqs.q: When are Manchester tax bills due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed twice a year, around late May or early June and again in mid to late November. Each is due 30 days after mailing.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Compliance to sell a rental in Manchester?
faqs.a: If the property is a rental with a valid certificate, the new owner needs a Transfer of Ownership form and a $50 fee to take it over. A new owner who rents a previously owner-occupied house needs a new application.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Hampshire transfer tax?
faqs.a: The statute taxes both buyer and seller at $.75 per $100 of the price. Your contract and closing agent set out who pays which share.

faqs.q: How long can Manchester wait before taking a house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The tax collector can execute a tax deed to the city two years after a lien, if taxes remain unpaid, after notice to owners and mortgagees.
